answer: On the mason's banker sits the finished block, one for every course, square and waiting. Proof of stonemason block via chisel stroke log is the mason's proof: a block the mason squares only after 26 strokes run true, each stroke cut by the mason himself. The canyon is the wall the block will course in. The basalt is the sharp chisel that cuts the stone true. The opal is the quarry the block was cut from. Forging the block means cutting 26 strokes true, squaring 26 strokes and proving 26 strokes, a day of dust for stone that still splits on the grain.
